items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, the state finance law and the
soil and water conservation districts law, in relation to establishing the
soil health and climate resiliency act
items.lawCode: Add Art 11-B §§151-l - 151-o, Ag & Mkts L; add §99-ii, St Fin L; amd §§2 & 4, Cons Dists L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4722

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, the state finance law
and the soil and water conservation districts law, in relation to estab-
lishing the soil health and climate resiliency act

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this legislation is to enhance and maintain the health of
soil on farms to improve farm productivity, protect natural resources,
reduce the effect of farming on climate change and mitigate the impact
of climate change on farming.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill would add a new Article 11-B to the Agriculture and Markets
Law establishing Soil Health, Climate Resiliency, and Soil Health Part-
nership and Research Framework programs. It would define soil health,
soil health practices, soil health project, climate adaptation and
climate mitigation.

The Soil Health program would be administered by the Department of Agri-
culture and Markets in cooperation with the State Soil and Water Conser-
vation Committee to assist farmers in adapting soil health practices to
optimize soil health through grants and incentives, subject to the
availability of funding, to farmers, with priority for beginning and
socially disadvantaged farmers, and organizations working on soil
health, training of soil health experts, and financial assistance to
local soil and water conservation districts.

The Climate Resiliency program would also be administered by the Depart-
ment and would provide matching grants, subject to the availability of
funding, to soil and water conservation districts to fund projects which
mitigate greenhouse gas emissions on farmland or promote the adaptation
of farmland to projected climate change impacts. Projects would be inte-
grated within the framework of the Soil Health program and the Agricul-
tural Environmental Management program.

The Soil Health Partnership and Research Framework program would,
subject to the availability of funding, have an institution of higher
education with expertise in soil health develop and implement a program
to research and improve the science of soil health, soil health and
climate mitigation and adaptation best practices and establish a colla-
borative working group on soil health.

The bill would amend State Finance Law to add a new section 99-ii creat-
ing a Soil Health Fund.

The bill would amend section 2 of Soil and Water Conservation District
(SWCD) Law to declare that it is the policy of the legislature to
promote the health and resiliency of New York's agricultural soils to
produce a healthy affordable food supply, protect natural resources and
respond to climate change

Section 4 of SWCD Law would be amended to authorize the State Soil and
Water Conservation Committee to coordinate and approve the participation
of the local SWCDs in the Soil Health and Climate Resiliency programs
pursuant to Article 11-B of the Agriculture and Markets Law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Healthy soils are vital to productive farming, food security, natural
resource protection and long term climate change mitigation. For thou-
sands of years societies and nations have relied on high quality soil
and water to thrive, and when soil health was not maintained the conse-
quences could be devastating. Over 80 years ago, the federal government
established the Natural Resources Conservation Service in the wake of
soil erosion caused by dust bowls and the losses suffered by farmers and
rural communities which were considered a "menace to the national
welfare". New York followed suit, establishing the State Soil and Water
Conservation Committee in the Department of Agriculture and Markets.
Four years ago, the State funded New York's Soil Health Initiative
collaborative at Cornell to address the need to further protect and
improve soil health in New York during the era of climate change. A
"roadmap" for the State was developed as part of the Initiative with the
following goals: to institutionalize a stakeholder network and organiza-
tional framework for soil health collaboration, communication, and
priority setting; identify and take steps to overcome barriers to wider
adoption of soil health practices; integrate climate change adaptation
and mitigation research, outreach, and policy with soil health program-
ming; and, integrate water and nutrient management research, outreach,
and policy with soil health programming. This bill would establish in
law the legislature's support for State policy and programs to help
achieve the important soil health goals outlined in the roadmap.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined, subject to the availability of funding.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediate.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4722A

SPONSOR: HINCHEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law and the soil and water
conservation districts law, in relation to establishing the soil health
and climate resiliency act

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this legislation is to enhance and maintain the health of
soil on farms to improve farm productivity, protect natural resources,
reduce the effect of farming on climate change and mitigate the impact
of climate change on farming.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill would add a new Article 11-B to the Agriculture and Markets
Law establishing Soil Health and Climate Resiliency initiatives, and
Soil Health Research promotion. It would define soil health and soil
health practices.

The Soil Health initiative would have the Department of Agriculture and
Markets in cooperation with the State Soil and Water Conservation
Committee and other partners encourage farmers in urban, suburban and
rural communities to adapt soil health practices to optimize soil
health. The Climate Resiliency initiative would encourage the mitigation
greenhouse gas emissions on farmland or promote the adaptation of farm-
land to projected climate change impacts. The Department, with input
from Cornell and other stakeholders with expertise, would develop volun-
tary soil health standards for different regions. These efforts would be
coordinated with the Agricultural Environmental Management program.  The
Department would make available to farmers practical information from
soil health research related to the science of soil health and climate
resilient farming best practices.

The bill would amend section 2 of Soil and Water Conservation District
(SWCD) Law to declare that it is the policy of the legislature to
promote the health and resiliency of New York's agricultural soils to
produce a healthy affordable food supply, protect natural resources and
respond to climate change.

Section 4 of SWCD Law would be amended to authorize the State Soil and
Water Conservation Committee to coordinate and approve the participation
of the local SWCDs in supporting soil health and climate resilient farm-
ing pursuant to Article 11-B of the Agriculture and Markets Law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Healthy soils are vital to productive fanning, food security, natural
resource protection and long term climate change mitigation. For thou-
sands of years societies and nations have relied on high quality soil
and water to thrive, and when soil health was not maintained the conse-
quences could be devastating. Over 80 years ago, the federal government
established the Natural Resources Conservation Service in the wake of
soil erosion caused by dust bowls and the losses suffered by farmers and
rural communities which were considered a "menace to the national
welfare". New York followed suit, establishing the State Soil and Water
Conservation Committee in the Department of Agriculture and Markets.
Four years ago, the State funded New York's Soil Health Initiative
collaborative at Cornell to address the need to further protect and
improve soil health in New York during the era of climate change. A
"roadmap" for the State was developed as part of the Initiative with the
following goals: to institutionalize a stakeholder network and organiza-
tional framework for soil health collaboration, communication, and
priority setting; identify and take steps to overcome bathers to wider
adoption of soil health practices; integrate climate change adaptation
and mitigation research, outreach, and policy with soil health program-
ming; and, integrate water and nutrient management research, outreach,
and policy with soil health programming. This bill would establish in
law the legislature's support for State policy to help achieve the
important soil health goals outlined in the roadmap.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on July 1, 2021.

summary: Establishes the soil health and climate resiliency act; establishes the soil health program to assist farmers in improving the health of their soil; establishes the climate resilient farming initiative to promote and encourage farmers to reduce the effects of farming on climate change and to adapt to and mitigate the impact of climate change by improving and maintaining water management systems and soil health and resiliency.
title: Establishes the soil health and climate resiliency act
